source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
Vine pruning is done to direct the plant's growth toward a limited number of main vines so that nutrients and energy are concentrated into productive vines and fruit rather than being spread across excess side branches. Farmers typically pinch off the growing tip of the main vine once it has produced around leaf 5 to 6, which encourages the plant to branch and select the strongest side shoots to become the productive fruiting vines, and continue removing weaker or excess side shoots afterward so the plant channels its growth and nutrients into the retained vines.

Watermelon vines may either be left to trail/spread along the ground on the mulched bed (the traditional method for field production) or trained up a support structure/trellis (poles and wire or twine) in some intensive or protected-growing systems, which keeps developing fruit off the soil, improves air circulation, reduces disease contact with wet ground, and can make it easier to monitor fruit and remove diseased or damaged leaves.
